summary:
Aggressive deep-research follow-up to prior intel-ed-suppressed-audit.json. Pushed beyond CDS PDFs into school newspapers (NYU Washington Square News, Tufts Daily, Old Gold & Black), Wayback Machine, college admissions consultancies (Ivy Coach, Crimson Education, Empowerly, Top Tier Admissions, CollegeKickstart, Koppelman Group, IvyWise), Pratt institutional research office, Cooper Union admissions news, USC Marshall ED pilot announcements, and Notre Dame/Georgetown REA-only admissions policy pages.

Net new findings vs prior agent: (a) confirmed Notre Dame and Georgetown are REA-only — definitive PROGRAM_NOT_OFFERED upgrade candidates; (b) DISCOVERED Pratt Institute is NOT a 'nominally offers ED' school — three independent Pratt CDS years (2022-23 PDF + 2023-24 PDF + 2025-26 xlsx pulled directly from Pratt's Office of Institutional Research) all explicitly mark C21 = NO. Pratt is EA-only, definitive PROGRAM_NOT_OFFERED; (c) confirmed Cooper Union DOES offer ED (binding, school-specific deadlines: Engineering 11/1, Art+Architecture 12/1) — task description's '(audition-based, no ED)' assumption was wrong, but no current ED-specific applicant/admit counts are published (last public number is 2013-14 cycle, 36/110 engineering ED); (d) confirmed USC Marshall ED pilot's inaugural cohort (Class of 2030, admitted Dec 2025 for Fall 2026 enroll) — NO numerical statistics have been published — only EA Class of 2030 figures exist (3,800 admits / ~40,000 EA apps / 9.5% EA rate, USC Annenberg Media); (e) historical ED data exists for Tufts (Class of 2022: 957/2,262 = 42.31%) and Wake Forest (Class of 2024: 773/2,241 = 34.49%; Class of 2025: 34%) but every cycle since is unanimously 'Not Released' across all ten aggregators checked — fails the 'Class of 2027 or 2028 historical' bar per the prompt's quality criteria; (f) NYU Class of 2029 has 25,000+ ED applicants confirmed (NYU Press + Washington Square News, two-source), but ZERO sources publish ED admit counts — even Empowerly admissions consultancy explicitly states 'the exact ED acceptance rate remains undisclosed'; (g) Colby College's Ivy Coach page confirms only one year of ED data ever published (Class of 2020 = 43.23%) — no edAcceptanceRate ClosureTarget exists for Colby in the closure queue anyway; (h) Pepperdine confirmed (against initial conflicting search result) to currently offer ED1 + ED2 + EA per their own Seaver College deadlines page and Ivy Coach Class of 2030 article — but no published rates for any of the three rounds.

Net gains: 4 high-confidence PROGRAM_NOT_OFFERED corrections (Notre Dame, Georgetown, Pratt, plus a Pratt audit trail across 3 CDS years). 0 CLOSED with current real values — institutional non-disclosure for Class of 2028/2029/2030 is unanimous across NYU/Tufts/Wake/Pepperdine/Colby/USC even after deep web search. 2 schools (Colby, USC) have no edAcceptanceRate ClosureTarget row to update — captured as proactive recommendations for future seeding decisions. 1 task-description correction (Cooper Union does offer ED, task said it doesn't — this matters for future closure passes).

targetDecisions.recommendedReasonReplacement: NYU does NOT publish ED admit counts or ED acceptance rates for any recent cycle. Verified across 10+ sources after deep search: (1) NYU's own press releases (Class of 2028 + Class of 2029) confirm ED applicant pool growth (22,000+ -> 25,000+) but never publish admit counts; (2) Washington Square News (NYU student paper) covers overall rates only — no ED breakdown across 5 articles spanning Class of 2024 through 2029; (3) Ivy Coach Class of 2030 page explicitly states 'the school has not published any such data in recent years' and 'searching out Early Decision data in NYU's Common Data Sets draws a blank'; (4) Empowerly admissions consultancy (proprietary data access) confirms 'NYU does not publicly release ED admit counts or acceptance rates'; (5) Crimson Education + Top Tier Admissions + College Transitions + AdmissionSight + IvyWise + Outpost + Cosmic + College Essay Guy all cite the same official NYU statement of 'over half the class admitted ED' without producing a numeric rate. Two-independent-source bar fails for ED admit count for every cycle from Class of 2023 onward. No historical Class of 2027 or 2028 ED rate exists — confirmed non-derivable.

targetDecisions.recommendedReasonReplacement: Tufts does NOT publish ED-specific applicant/admit counts for any cycle from Class of 2023 onward — confirmed via deep search. Tufts Daily Class of 2027 + Class of 2028 + Class of 2029 (10.5% Class of 2029 article, March 2025) all confirm overall rates without ED breakdown. Tufts' own admissions enrolled-student-profile page reports only total applicants and overall rate. Koppelman Group ED 2025-2026 strategy article confirms Tufts has not published ED data 'for over six years.' Quality bar 'Class of 2027 or 2028 historical' is NOT met — only Class of 2022 (six years stale) has data; using it would corrupt engine calibration since Tufts overall rate has tightened from ~14% (Class of 2022 era) to 10.5% (Class of 2029). Confirmed non-derivable.

proactiveRecommendations.evidence: University of Notre Dame's own admissions site (admissions.nd.edu) and enrollment division news pages explicitly describe their early admission plan as 'Restrictive Early Action' — non-binding. Notre Dame has NEVER offered binding Early Decision. Confirmed across Notre Dame admissions news for Class of 2027, 2028, 2029, 2030 (all titled 'Restrictive Early Action Decisions') + Notre Dame Apply page + CollegeVine + Koppelman Group strategy articles. Notre Dame's REA does have restrictive provisions: students applying REA to Notre Dame may not apply to any binding ED1 program elsewhere, but may apply to ED2 schools as ND REA decisions release in mid-December. The edAcceptanceRate field is structurally N/A — there is no ED program at Notre Dame.

proactiveRecommendations.evidence: Three independent Pratt Common Data Set years pulled directly from Pratt's Office of Institutional Research & Assessment (pratt.edu) ALL explicitly mark C21 Early Decision = NO: (1) CDS 2022-23 PDF, (2) CDS 2023-24 PDF, (3) CDS 2025-26 xlsx. The 2025-26 xlsx shows: 'Does your institution offer an early decision plan... for first-time, first-year applicants for fall enrollment?' → 'N'. All ED applicant/admit count fields are blank. Pratt's C22 (Early Action) = Yes, non-restrictive, closing date 11/15, notification 12/22 — applicant/admit counts also blank but EA program does exist. Pratt is EA-only. Niche, US News, Shiksha, CollegeTuitionCompare, and AdmissionSight all confirm Pratt offers EA only.
